post.description: Search matches franchises and standalone series by title.
ListCatalog pages through every top-level entry as a flat summary row.
GetFranchise returns one franchise with each of its series embedded whole.

GetCharacter returns one character by id, with every appearance and the
 voice actors cast for it.
ListCharacters returns the whole cast, or just one series' cast.
GetStaff returns one staff member by id with every role they are cast in.

ListStaff returns every staff member, optionally filtered by the language
 they are credited in.
GetStats reports what the dataset contains, plus the deployed revision.

anime.v1.ReleaseSeason.title: ReleaseSeason
anime.v1.ReleaseSeason.description:
ReleaseSeason is the calendar quarter an installment premiered in.

 The values are unprefixed so the JSON reads "SPRING" — the same string the
 dataset stores — rather than "RELEASE_SEASON_SPRING", which every client was
 left to translate back. Protobuf scopes enum values to the package, so a
 prefix is added only where the bare word would collide with another enum's
 (see SpecialFormat).
 buf:lint:ignore ENUM_VALUE_PREFIX

anime.v1.SpecialFormat.title: SpecialFormat
anime.v1.SpecialFormat.description:
SpecialFormat is the kind of side content a Special represents. Prefixed,
 because SPECIAL alone would collide with the browse API's WorkKind.
 buf:lint:ignore ENUM_VALUE_PREFIX

browse.v1.EntryKind.title: EntryKind
browse.v1.EntryKind.description:
EntryKind distinguishes a top-level catalog entry's type: the dataset's
 browsable roots are franchises and the series that belong to none.
 buf:lint:ignore ENUM_VALUE_PREFIX

anime.v1.AlternateCutOf.title: AlternateCutOf
anime.v1.AlternateCutOf.description: AlternateCutOf links an alternate-cut film to the Season it re-cuts.

name.title: name
name.description:
name is resolved for the request's Accept-Language, by the same rules as
 a title. Empty when the dataset carries no name for the character yet.

localizedName.title: localized_name
localizedName.description: localized_name carries every language; set only for Accept-Language: *.

voiceActors.title: voice_actors
voiceActors.description:
voice_actors is the cast that holds throughout — an original-language role
 is nearly always the same person in every adaptation. Cast that varies by
 series (English dubs are routinely recast) is not here; it is on the
 appearance it belongs to. An appearance's voice_actors already includes
 these, so a client showing per-appearance cast never needs this field.

appearances.title: appearances
appearances.description: appearances is every series this character appears in.

anime.v1.Character.title: Character
anime.v1.Character.description: Character is a global fictional entity, owned by no Franchise or Series.

seriesTitle.title: series_title
seriesTitle.description:
series_title is that series' title resolved for the request's
 Accept-Language, denormalized for the same reason VoiceActor carries
 staff_name: a client rendering a character's appearances should not have to
 call GetSeries once per appearance to label them.

voiceActors.title: voice_actors
voiceActors.description:
voice_actors is the cast for this appearance, resolved: it is the
 character's constant cast plus whoever is specific to that series. Render
 it as-is; there is nothing to merge client-side.

anime.v1.CharacterAppearance.title: CharacterAppearance
anime.v1.CharacterAppearance.description:
CharacterAppearance is a Character <-> Series edge. series_id is the rollup
 association and scope optionally narrows it to specific installments.

 A character reached through GetSeries is the full global node, so its
 appearances may name series other than the one you asked for. That is how a
 caller learns a character is shared across the catalogue.

anime.v1.Episode.title: Episode
anime.v1.Episode.description:
Episode is one numbered entry of a season or special.

 It carries numbering and nothing else. The upstream database publishes an
 episode *count*, not a list, so the entries are the count expanded to 1..n;
 aired_number is that position and absolute_number is the franchise-wide
 running count assignAbsoluteNumbers computes by interleaving installments in
 release order, which is the one fact here that is not arithmetic.

 3 and 4 held release_date and title. Both were declared before there was a
 source for them and neither was ever populated — 0 of 3,229 episodes — so
 the API advertised fields that always came back empty. They are removed
 rather than left as an intention: if an episode-level source is ever added,
 filling a new field is easier than explaining a permanently blank one.

anime.v1.ExternalIds.title: ExternalIds
anime.v1.ExternalIds.description: ExternalIds cross-maps a node to external databases. All fields are optional.

anime.v1.LocalizedTitle.title: LocalizedTitle
anime.v1.LocalizedTitle.description:
LocalizedTitle holds a title across languages: the original native-script
 form plus translations keyed by BCP-47 code (en, ja, ...).

 Every title-bearing message carries a resolved `title` (a single string for
 the request's Accept-Language, defaulting to English) plus this full
 `localized_title`. To keep responses small, `localized_title` is populated
 ONLY when the client sends `Accept-Language: *`; otherwise just `title` is
 returned. See AnimeService for the language-resolution rules.

title.title: title
title.description: title is resolved for the request's Accept-Language.

localizedTitle.title: localized_title
localizedTitle.description: localized_title carries every language; set only for Accept-Language: *.

anime.v1.Movie.title: Movie
anime.v1.Movie.description: Movie is one film (one media node).

title.title: title
title.description:
title is that installment's own title resolved for the request's
 Accept-Language, denormalized for the same reason series_title is: a client
 labelling a scoped appearance should not have to look the installment up.
 A numbered season usually has no title of its own, so number carries its
 position for a caller composing a label; it is 0 for a movie or special.

anime.v1.ScopeRef.title: ScopeRef
anime.v1.ScopeRef.description:
ScopeRef narrows a CharacterAppearance to one installment of a Series.
 Exactly one id field is set.

title.title: title
title.description: title is resolved for the request's Accept-Language.

localizedTitle.title: localized_title
localizedTitle.description: localized_title carries every language; set only for Accept-Language: *.

episodes.title: episodes
episodes.description: episodes is every episode of this season, in order.

anime.v1.Season.title: Season
anime.v1.Season.description: Season is one numbered TV installment (one media node / cour).

title.title: title
title.description: title is resolved for the request's Accept-Language.

localizedTitle.title: localized_title
localizedTitle.description: localized_title carries every language; set only for Accept-Language: *.

characters.title: characters
characters.description:
characters is this series' whole cast, in dataset order. Each is the full
 global Character node, so its appearances may name other series too.

anime.v1.Series.title: Series
anime.v1.Series.description:
Series is the unit of this API: one storyline / continuity, whole.

 Every collection below is complete — no caps, no page tokens, no companion
 List calls. One series is bounded by what a series can be: the longest-running
 show in existence is a four-figure episode count of two integers each, and a
 large cast is a few hundred names. The thing this API refuses to serialize
 unbounded is a *collection of series*, which is what SearchSeries pages.

title.title: title
title.description: title is resolved for the request's Accept-Language.

localizedTitle.title: localized_title
localizedTitle.description: localized_title carries every language; set only for Accept-Language: *.

episodes.title: episodes
episodes.description: episodes is every episode of this special, in order.

anime.v1.Special.title: Special
anime.v1.Special.description: Special is one OVA / ONA / special (side content, no season number).

staffName.title: staff_name
staffName.description:
staff_name is the staff member's name resolved for the request's
 Accept-Language, denormalized so a client need not look the person up.
 Empty when the dataset carries no name for them yet.

throughout.title: throughout
throughout.description:
throughout marks a credit that comes from the character rather than from
 the thing being described — Ayako Kawasumi voices Saber in every Fate
 work, so she is `throughout` in each of Saber's appearances while the
 English dub cast alongside her is not.

 It is set only on an appearance's cast, where the two are mixed. Ignore it
 and you still have the full cast, which is the point of resolving the list
 server-side; read it and you can tell what is specific to one series
 without diffing two lists yourself.

anime.v1.VoiceActor.title: VoiceActor
anime.v1.VoiceActor.description: VoiceActor links a Character to the Staff who voices it in one language.

title.title: title
title.description: title is resolved for the request's Accept-Language.

localizedTitle.title: localized_title
localizedTitle.description: localized_title carries every language; set only for Accept-Language: *.

franchiseId.title: franchise_id
franchiseId.description:
franchise_id is set when kind is SERIES and the series belongs to a
 franchise; empty for a standalone series or a franchise entry.

firstReleaseYear.title: first_release_year
firstReleaseYear.description:
The span of release years across everything under this entry. Both are 0
 when nothing under it carries a year.

works.title: works
works.description: Counts of what sits under this entry: works is seasons + movies + specials.

browse.v1.CatalogEntry.title: CatalogEntry
browse.v1.CatalogEntry.description:
CatalogEntry is one browsable top-level entry — a franchise or a standalone
 series — carrying just enough to render a catalog row. It nests nothing, so a
 page stays small however large the catalog grows.

earliestReleaseYear.title: earliest_release_year
earliestReleaseYear.description:
The span of release years the dataset actually covers, across every work
 that carries a year. Both are 0 for an empty dataset.

title.title: title
title.description: title is resolved for the request's Accept-Language.

localizedTitle.title: localized_title
localizedTitle.description: localized_title carries every language; set only for Accept-Language: *.

browse.v1.Franchise.title: Franchise
browse.v1.Franchise.description:
Franchise groups related Series under one brand.

 series embeds each member whole, exactly as anime.v1.GetSeries returns it, so
 a franchise page renders in one call. That is affordable because a franchise
 holds a handful of series; if one ever holds dozens, this is the field to
 reconsider — and being internal, it can be changed without notice.

credits.title: credits
credits.description:
credits is every role this person is cast in, in dataset order. A career is
 bounded the way a series is, so this is embedded whole rather than paged.

version.title: version
version.description:
version is the deployed revision, so a caller can tell which build
 answered.

kind.title: kind
kind.description:
kind restricts the result to franchises or to standalone series;
 unspecified returns both.

seriesId.title: series_id
seriesId.description:
series_id restricts the result to that series' cast; empty lists every
 character in the dataset. It also decides what each character's
 voice_actors means: with a series, they are that series' cast (the constant
 cast plus anyone cast only there); without one, only the cast that holds
 throughout.

query.title: query
query.description:
query matches a character's name in any language, case-insensitively, as a
 substring. Empty matches every character.

language.title: language
language.description:
language restricts the result to staff credited in that language ("ja");
 empty lists everyone. It chooses *which people* come back, not what
 language their names are written in — that is Accept-Language, and the two
 are deliberately separate.

query.title: query
query.description:
query matches a staff member's name in any language, case-insensitively,
 as a substring. Empty matches everyone.

limit.title: limit
limit.description: limit caps the number of results; <= 0 applies a server default.

pageToken.title: page_token
pageToken.description: page_token continues a previous call; empty starts from the beginning.

title.title: title
title.description: title is resolved for the request's Accept-Language.

localizedTitle.title: localized_title
localizedTitle.description: localized_title carries every language; set only for Accept-Language: *.

franchiseId.title: franchise_id
franchiseId.description:
franchise_id is set when kind is SERIES and the series belongs to a
 franchise; empty for a standalone series or a franchise result.

browse.v1.SearchResult.title: SearchResult
browse.v1.SearchResult.description: SearchResult is one match: a top-level franchise or a standalone series.

name.title: name
name.description: name is resolved for the request's Accept-Language.

localizedName.title: localized_name
localizedName.description: localized_name carries every language; set only for Accept-Language: *.

browse.v1.Staff.title: Staff
browse.v1.Staff.description: Staff is a global real person — currently only voice actors.

seriesTitles.title: series_titles
seriesTitles.description:
series_titles are those series' titles resolved for the request's
 Accept-Language, positionally matching series_ids, so a page listing
 someone's roles can name each one without a call per credit.

browse.v1.StaffCredit.title: StaffCredit
browse.v1.StaffCredit.description:
StaffCredit is one role a Staff member is cast in: the character they voice,
 the language they voice it in, and the series it applies to.

browse.v1.WatchOrder.title: WatchOrder
browse.v1.WatchOrder.description: WatchOrder is a named curated alternate order across a Franchise's Series.

browse.v1.WatchOrderEntry.title: WatchOrderEntry
browse.v1.WatchOrderEntry.description:
WatchOrderEntry is one ordered reference within a WatchOrder. ref is the id
 of a series, season, movie or special, validated against the dataset at build
 time (see builder/internal/build/validate.go).

connect-protocol-version.title: Connect-Protocol-Version
connect-protocol-version.description: Define the version of the Connect protocol

code.description: The status code, which should be an enum value of [google.rpc.Code][google.rpc.Code].

message.description: A developer-facing error message, which should be in English. Any user-facing error message should be localized and sent in the [google.rpc.Status.details][google.rpc.Status.details] field, or localized by the client.

google.protobuf.Any.description: Contains an arbitrary serialized message along with a @type that describes the type of the serialized message.

BrowseService serves anime-metadata-web. See the package comment: undocumented
 by design, and free to change with the site.
